target_customer: Software developers and construction software vendors who needed API access to contractor systems at founding; later general and trade contractors that buy back-office automation
problem: Construction financial and project systems were old, often on-premises and without usable APIs, so connecting them or automating invoice, expense and compliance work was manual.
business_model: Usage and subscription pricing for a unified API at founding, later B2B SaaS and AI back-office agents sold to contractors
product_category: Construction unified API, then AI financial operations for contractors

founders.name: Tom Reno
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; employer list as stated there.

founders.name: Pooria Azimi
education: Oregon State University, master's in computer science
founders.background_notes: Core engineer at Graphiq per YC page.

founders.name: John Zucchi
founders.background_notes: Technical program manager at Alexa and product manager at Graphiq per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading and writing across dozens of legacy and on-premises construction ERPs without APIs or documentation required reverse engineering and per-system connectors (33 systems and 950 endpoints by the 2023 seed per TechCrunch).

defensibility.rationale: Each connector is slow to build and partnerships with platforms add friction, but platforms such as Procore control API terms, and the company says it spent four years on proprietary two way connections.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Trimble bought the iPaaS vendor Ryvit (now DataXchange) and Procore built a large partner marketplace; in 2025 Procore tightened API terms, which affected startups using Agave connectors. Agave itself stayed independent.

market_need_then: Construction runs on financial software built decades ago, much of it on premises without APIs, so vendors and contractors lacked a way to integrate; Agave's seed coverage cites demand for a single API across project management, ERP and scheduling.

branding.domain_note: Uses useagave.com, not the exact .com; search results for the word are dominated by the plant and spirits.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B positioning around construction accounting

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the name is a common word shared with tequila and mezcal coverage, so search confusion is likely, and no mascot or community was found.

pivots.from: Unified API for developers to read and write construction software data
pivots.to: AI agents for contractor back-office financial work (applied AI for construction)
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; product pages and the July 2026 Series A release show the move to AI invoice matching, expenses and compliance. The exact date is not given.

outcome_analysis: Agave started as a unified API for construction software, took a small seed from Accel in August 2023, and moved toward AI back-office agents, announcing a $15M Series A in July 2026 with Accel and YC both reinvesting. The hard integration work with legacy systems is its main asset, while platform risk from Procore API terms in 2025 is the main threat. It is active with no exit.
notes: Seed amount and Series A amount are from press coverage (TechCrunch snippet, a Business Wire based release carried by pulse2) and cross-checked against an aggregator snippet; I did not open the TechCrunch page itself. YC page says founded 2021; one profile says 2020. Founder education was only given where the YC page states it. The outcome search returned only agave plant news, so no negative event was found. No dated competitor sources near the W22 batch were found; later context (Procore terms 2025, Trimble Ryvit) is in takeover_risk_then. Co-founder Tom Reno education not stated.
